summary: This is the cleaned-up JUnit test class for the TrafficLight from earlier in the chapter. Each test method now checks a single fact about the light "Red" "Green" "Yellow" "Red" "Green" "Yellow" — its starting color, one step of advancement, or whether a stop is required at a particular color.

lines.text: The original version crammed every color check into one method, so a failure told you nothing about which case broke. Splitting it out means the starting state gets its own named test that can fail on its own.

This asserts the real value the light should hold, rather than merely confirming that a color exists at all. A test that only checks for the presence of something will pass even when the value is wrong.
The color is only a label; the behavior drivers care about is whether they must stop. Testing isStopRequired covers the decision the class actually makes.

Each advancement test does the setup calls, then makes exactly one call as the action being tested, then asserts. That structure keeps the test from re-creating the cycle logic that TrafficLight already owns.
Verifying that yellow wraps back around to red proves the cycle closes, which is the one place a color-advancing class most often gets it wrong.
